**DI62** is a medical diagnosis code used in the Danish healthcare system to identify "other non-traumatic intracranial hemorrhages" (andre ikke-traumatiske intrakranielle blødninger) [^src1]. It plays a critical role in tracking the safety and clinical outcomes of patients diagnosed with [[atrieflimren|atrial fibrillation]] [^src1]. Specifically, the code is utilized within the clinical quality indicators managed by the Regionernes Kliniske Kvalitetsudviklingsprogram (RKKP) to measure the incidence of [[intrakraniel-bloedning|intracranial bleeding]] and severe bleeding events among these patient populations [^src1].

In the context of the national atrial fibrillation databases, DI62 is grouped with several other diagnostic codes to capture a comprehensive picture of bleeding complications. For measuring the specific incidence of intracranial bleeding, DI62 is used alongside [[di60|DI60]], [[di61|DI61]], [[ds064|DS064]], [[ds065|DS065]], and [[ds066|DS066]] [^src1]. Furthermore, when evaluating the broader incidence of severe bleeding—a key safety metric for anticoagulation therapy—DI62 is included in a wide array of codes that also track gastrointestinal bleeding (such as [[dk25-0|DK25.0]] through [[dk29-8a|DK29.8A]] and [[dk92-0|DK92.0]] through [[dk92-2|DK92.2]]) and urinary or respiratory tract bleeding (including [[dj942|DJ942]], [[dn02|DN02]], [[dr04|DR04]], and [[dr31|DR31]]) [^src1]. These standardized codes ensure consistent data collection from the Danish National Patient Register and allow for rigorous comparison of treatment safety across different regions [^src2].
